findings.issue: Task 7 declares `depends_on: [6]` and treats FunnelTriggersPanel.vue as a Task-6 output it can immediately consume. The component does NOT exist yet (`frontend/components/funnels/FunnelTriggersPanel.vue` — not found on disk). If Task 6 has not been executed before Task 7 runs, the consumer will fail to import the panel.
findings.fix: This is expected by design (depends_on [6] is declared). Validate that Task 6 is marked done and the file exists on disk BEFORE Task 7 execution begins. The task file itself is correct — execution harness must enforce the dependency gate.

findings.issue: Task 7 instructs 'read the FunnelTriggersPanel.vue contract before wiring' (Context Files, Implementation Hints). The file does not exist at `frontend/components/funnels/FunnelTriggersPanel.vue`. The task cannot read the actual prop/event contract of the panel before implementation because Task 6 has not yet run. This creates a real risk: Task 7 may guess the prop contract and produce an integration mismatch.
findings.fix: Add an explicit pre-condition note: 'Do not start this task until `frontend/components/funnels/FunnelTriggersPanel.vue` exists on disk. Read that file first to discover the exact v-model / props / events interface before writing any wiring code.' The dependency is declared but not emphasised in the What-to-do guard.

findings.issue: Task 7 references `FunnelResponse.triggers` in `applyResponse()`/`load()` (e.g., 'populate `triggers` from `res.triggers`'). The actual `FunnelResponse` interface in `frontend/types/funnel.ts` (line 169-184) has NO `triggers` field — it still carries the flat trio `triggerType`, `triggerValue`, `keywords`. These fields must be added by Task 6 (or Task 3 frontend side). Task 7 treats `res.triggers` as already available, but if Task 6 has not been executed the type does not carry it and TypeScript will error. The task correctly states 'Task 6 updates types' but does not tell the implementer to read `types/funnel.ts` after Task 6 runs to verify the actual field name before using it.
findings.fix: Add a guard: 'Before writing `applyResponse()`, read `frontend/types/funnel.ts` to confirm `FunnelResponse.triggers` (or its actual field name as Task 6 defined it) exists. If the field name differs from `triggers`, adjust accordingly.' The task should not hard-code `res.triggers` as a fact — the implementer must verify.

findings.issue: Task 7 TDD Anchor lists five test cases for `frontend/tests/pages/funnel-editor.spec.ts`, all inside a new block. The existing `draft()` factory (line 61-77 of funnel-editor.spec.ts) returns `FunnelResponse` with `triggerType`/`triggerValue`/`keywords` flat fields — NOT a `triggers: [...]` array. The task says 'Update `draft()` factory: return `triggers: [...]` instead of the flat trio', but `FunnelResponse` in `types/funnel.ts` currently has no `triggers` field. The factory update is contingent on Task 6 changing the type. If the implementer writes new tests using `draft({ triggers: [...] })` against the un-updated type, TypeScript will fail to compile the spec file. The task treats this as a simple edit but it's actually a compile-time dependency on Task 6's type changes.
findings.fix: Emphasise in TDD Anchor: 'The draft() factory update requires `FunnelResponse.triggers` to exist in `types/funnel.ts` (Task 6 output). Confirm the type before writing or running new tests. If types/funnel.ts still has the flat trio, Task 6 is incomplete — do not proceed.'

findings.issue: Task 7 Implementation Hints claim the `<FunnelTriggerSettings v-model:.../>` block is at 'lines ~445-451' of `[funnelId].vue`. The actual file confirms `FunnelTriggerSettings` is indeed at line 445 with the flat v-model bindings (verified). However, the hint says the replacement is `<FunnelTriggersPanel v-model="triggers" :bot-username="botUsername" :deep-link="funnel.deepLink" :steps="steps" />` — but `funnel.deepLink` is accessed as a nullable string off the `FunnelResponse` ref. Since `funnel` is `ref<FunnelResponse | null>`, the template must guard against null (`:deep-link="funnel?.deepLink"` or inside the `v-else` block). The existing template is inside `<div v-else class="space-y-6">` (line 332) so `funnel` is non-null in scope — this is actually fine. The hint is slightly misleading about null-safety but not wrong in context.
findings.fix: Minor: clarify hint as ':deep-link="funnel.deepLink" (safe — this block is inside v-else where funnel is non-null)'. No code change required.

findings.issue: The existing `trigger auto-save readiness` test block in `funnel-editor.spec.ts` (lines 176-270+) uses `data-test` selectors like `funnel-trigger-type-select`, `funnel-trigger-keyword-input`, `funnel-trigger-keyword-add`, `funnel-trigger-event-input`, `funnel-trigger-value-input` that belong to `FunnelTriggerSettings.vue`. After Task 7, these UI elements live inside `FunnelTriggersPanel.vue` (Task 6 output). The task says 'selectors will move to FunnelTriggersPanel (Task 6) — reconcile with them; do not leave dead selectors'. However, the task gives NO guidance on what the new selectors will be (since `FunnelTriggersPanel.vue` does not exist yet). The TDD Anchor tests WILL fail not just on logic but on missing `data-test` selectors if the panel uses different attribute names. There is a real risk of the tests being rewritten to stub the panel entirely (negating their value) rather than testing through actual rendered elements.
findings.fix: Add a note: 'After Task 6 runs, grep `FunnelTriggersPanel.vue` for `data-test` attributes and reconcile the test selectors with actual rendered elements. Do NOT stub `FunnelTriggersPanel` in these tests — they must render through the real component to catch wiring bugs. If the panel uses `data-test="funnel-trigger-type-select"` etc., the existing tests may work as-is; verify before rewriting them wholesale.'

findings.issue: The Implementation Hints section provides a nearly-complete template replacement block: `<FunnelTriggersPanel v-model="triggers" :bot-username="botUsername" :deep-link="funnel.deepLink" :steps="steps" />`. This prescribes the exact prop names (`v-model`, `:bot-username`, `:deep-link`, `:steps`) before the implementer has read the actual Task-6 component contract. The hint itself says 'take the exact prop form from the Task-6 component contract' — the contradiction weakens the hint and may cause the implementer to cargo-cult the hint rather than reading the actual file. This is an overspecified hint that prescribes the solution instead of pointing at the pattern.
findings.fix: Replace the concrete prop list with: 'Read `FunnelTriggersPanel.vue` (Task 6 output) — look for defineProps and defineEmits to discover the exact interface. Wire accordingly. The component likely expects the triggers array via v-model and a steps list for the entry-step picker.'

findings.issue: Task 7 says 'remove the unused import `FunnelTriggerSettings`' after replacing it with `FunnelTriggersPanel`. The existing page (line 15) imports `FunnelTriggerSettings from '~/components/funnels/FunnelTriggerSettings.vue'`. However, `FunnelTriggerSettings` is internally used INSIDE `FunnelTriggersPanel.vue` (tech-spec Decision 13: 'mounts FunnelTriggerSettings.vue per trigger'). The page import can safely be removed, but the note might confuse an implementer into thinking FunnelTriggerSettings is being retired — it is not, it moves inside the panel. This is clear in the Description but the Detail hint could be more precise.
findings.fix: Clarify: 'Remove the `FunnelTriggerSettings` import from the PAGE (line 15) — the component is now mounted internally by FunnelTriggersPanel.vue. Do not remove FunnelTriggerSettings.vue itself.'

This file's existence is not verified in this review, but Task 5 also lists it as a read-only dependency and uses the same path.
